title: Harness Engineering: The New Discipline of Agentic Dev
description:
Developers often discard most of their AI agent’s output, a method that seems wasteful but proves effective. By treating AI like a novice needing guidance, agentic development transforms workflows by centering tasks around a pivotal agent, akin to a crew rallying around a new recruit. It sounds wrong. It works. This approach creates a productive loop, emphasizing autonomy and allowing agents to deliver most of the end product by focusing on iterative feedback and improvements.

Daniel Jones, the head of product at re:cinq, provides insights into this method. Bringing his experience of leading multiple enterprises through the nuances of agentic development, Jones, in conversation with Simon Maple, shares hard-earned truths and unconventional practices that manage numerous agents effectively. Through their dialogue, they uncover techniques to extract valuable contributions without letting inefficiencies compound, underlining the role of good engineering practices in successful AI rollouts.

What we cover:
• Why engineering practices degrade with AI
• How agent hallucinations can be identified
• Is your AGENTS.md causing hidden issues
• What an enterprise AI rollout entails
• How poor management affects agentic coding
